text: p-sensitivity promises 'one injected defect per document gate', but sensitivity.py has 12 perturbations that cover 10 of the 13 document gates: p-anchor, p-size and p-sections were never perturbed, and neither were p-frozen-rubric (blocking) and p-notes. The validator only reads the 'Caught X of Y' line of sensitivity.md: it checks neither the coverage against the list of gates nor whether the file belongs to the current version of the documents, so the gate passes while its own definition is not met. A reviewer probe on a copy showed that the untested gates do reject the known defect; the gap is one of proof, not of behavior. Fix: add the missing perturbations and make the gate compare the set of perturbed gates with the gate table.
evidence: 04-gates-and-rubric.md, p-sensitivity row; 80-validator/sensitivity.py, PERTURBATIONS (lines 31-59); 80-validator/validator.py, check_global (reading of 'Caught X of Y'); reviewer probe on a copy: p-anchor 0, p-size 2334 words, p-sections 13/14 and p-frozen-rubric 'different' were rejected

text: The bible says the validator reads its tables ('changing a table changes what it checks') and that no case number enters a document without being in the 'Case numbers' table. The script does not read that table (load_bible loads the terms to avoid and the fixed lists), and p-case checks against the case method document. Result: two case numbers already in use are not in the table, 0.15 s (the drift limit, in the recipe) and 24 h (the recheck of volatile items, in the text instance). Both match the case method document; the defect is that the bible stops being the single source without any gate noticing. Fix: add the two numbers to the table and make p-case require that every [case] number be in it.
evidence: 01-bible.md, lines 4-5 and 172-174; validator.py, load_bible; 10-generic-recipe.md, lines 281-283; 21-instance-text-2027.md, line 278; case method document, section 1.10 and the table in section 2.4 (G1)

text: In the example 'Regression that escaped', the symptom is correct but serial work (8 and 16 threads take the same time, every result gate passes), but the indicated fix, 'divide by the number of threads the runtime gave, or use a work-sharing loop', fixes a different defect: the manual division by the requested number, which in a nested region with one thread processes only 1/k of the data and would fail equivalence. With a correct, serial region, what restores parallelism is removing the nesting (parallelizing at the outer level, collapsing loops) or enabling nested active levels. It is also missing where the obtained threads are measured: if they are read outside the region that does the work, h-obtained-configuration does not catch the case. Fix: align the fix with the symptom and declare the measurement point.
evidence: 22-instance-hpc.md, section 10, lines 358-363; section 3, 'measurements' schema (line 87); section 5, h-obtained-configuration row

text: The round loop examples contradict the instance's own initial state. According to the loop, h-obtained-configuration and h-counters 'are born' from a regression and from an instrument fix, but both are already in the gate table of section 5, in the CSV schema of section 3 and in the assembly engine of section 8 since the first version, so the counted regression could not have escaped. In addition, section 5 classifies the thread divergence as 'tool failure, not rejection', while the loop says the gate 'rejects the current version' and the cause is a product defect (note to the implementation). Fix: take the two gates out of the initial state and say they enter through the loop, or change the examples; and separate the divergence caused by the environment (tool failure) from the one caused by the library (rejection with a note to the implementation).
evidence: 22-instance-hpc.md, lines 87, 255, 260, 320-321, 358-367; experiment engineer role card, lines 179-180

text: The example 'Regression that escaped' says that 'the validator only read digits' and therefore gains the reading of numbers written out in words, but the validator table in section 7 already checks 'numbers written out ("one quarter", "two thirds")' from the start. text: The justification of t-source-density does not support the limit: it says books usually carry one footnote every 200 to 300 words in factual passages, that is, 3.3 to 5 per thousand, and calls 4 per thousand 'the floor, not the target'. Four is inside the typical range, above its lower end, not below it. Fix: lower the floor to something below the cited range (for example, 3 per thousand) or justify why the floor sits in the middle of it.
evidence: 21-instance-text-2027.md, section 5, line 273

text: The bible and the recipe itself define the orchestrator as a step that passes paths, runs the engine and imports notes, and say it 'decides nothing that a card assigns to a role'. Even so, the recipe makes it the author of the artifact list (step 4, with the brief's owner), of the role cards with decides and does not decide (step 5) and of the case method document (step 14). These artifacts are left without an owning role, which contradicts the 'Done when' of step 4 (every artifact with exactly one owner) and the practice of this work, in which the writer owns them. Fix: name an owning role (writer, process architect) for these steps and leave only execution to the orchestrator.
evidence: 01-bible.md, term 'orchestrator'; 10-generic-recipe.md, lines 74-76, 188, 213, 451; 02-artifacts.md, owners of artifacts and cards

text: Undeclared reflexivity gap. Step 8 of the recipe says the rubric is written by the 'owner, with whoever will review; never whoever will produce alone'. In this work, gates-and-rubric, which contains the rubric, is owned by the writer, the same role that wrote everything the rubric measures, and no document records the participation of the owner or the reviewer nor declares the deviation. Fix: declare the deviation in the brief, as was done with the owner decisions that have no file of their own, or record who approved the rubric before it was frozen.
evidence: 10-generic-recipe.md, step 8, line 291; 02-artifacts.md, gates-and-rubric row (owner: writer); 00-brief.md, 'Owner decisions' table (without the rubric)
